MENG LIM.name: Meng Lim
MENG LIM.background: Born in Cambodia shortly before the 1975 Khmer Rouge takeover. Survived labor camps as a child and came to the U.S. through Thai refugee camps; the family resettled in College Park and then Bremen. State wrestling champion and valedictorian at Bremen High School. History degree from Emory University; law degree from Mercer Law School. After clerking, he joined the law firm of House Speaker Tom Murphy, then opened a private practice with a family-law focus and served as attorney for the Haralson County Commission. Won a July 2014 runoff against Chuck Morris (62%) for the open Tallapoosa Judicial Circuit Superior Court seat (Haralson and Polk counties); he was the first Cambodian-American on a Georgia Superior Court bench. Re-elected unopposed in 2018. Lost to Andrew Roper in May 2022 and left the bench.
MENG LIM.record: In July 2020 he was arrested on a misdemeanor family-violence battery charge and voluntarily suspended from judicial office; Judge Mark Murphy took over the circuit's administrative duties. A Haralson County grand jury later threw out the domestic-violence charges, but Judicial Qualifications Commission charges remained open, per Polk Today. In the May 2022 election Andrew Roper defeated him (Polk Today's preliminary count: Roper 6,606, 61%, to Lim 4,207, 39%). Lim then resigned before his term ended.
